references.text: The Lord proclaims His name and character to Moses, describing Himself as merciful and gracious—a direct fulfillment of the promise in Exodus 34:6.
The Lord says that Moses has found favor in His sight, which is the context for God's promise to show His goodness.
God reveals His name to Moses at the burning bush, an earlier revelation of the Lord's name.
Paul quotes directly from this verse to explain God's sovereign grace and mercy—that it does not depend on human will or effort.
Paul continues his exposition of God's sovereign right to show mercy to whom He wills.
In the Ten Commandments, God describes Himself as one who shows mercy to thousands of generations—an expression of His merciful character.
The psalm describes the Lord as merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love—a reflection of God's self-revelation.
The Lord is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and great in lovingkindness. The Lord is good to all.
Jonah quotes God's character as gracious and merciful, a tradition stemming from the revelation given to Moses.
Moses prays to the Lord and cites His character as slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, based on the revelation in Exodus 34:6.
A direct quotation confirming and expanding upon God's sovereign right to choose whom He shows mercy toward.
A direct continuation of the same event; Exodus 34:6 elaborates on the character of the grace and mercy mentioned in Exodus 34:19.
